589d79e40a45.title: Judge Lets Hacker Behind Massive GTA 6 Leak of 2022 Go Free With a Warning: 'Don't Let This Happen Again'
589d79e40a45.summary: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge.
589d79e40a45.content: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally. According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again." Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week. ⚖️ Arion Kurtaj, 21, has been convicted today for targeting major international companies, hacking into their private systems, stealing information and data, and causing millions of dollars in losses. 📰 https://t.co/UvJTCFWnct https://t.co/3CoLIw7dDs — Crown Prosecution Service (@CPSUK) November 16, 2026 Originally, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a prison hospital due to his autism diagnosis. After reconsideration, he was deemed fit to stand trial and spent the remainder of his time in a traditional prison, starting in January. With his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his interactions online, barring him from using social apps like Telegram and Discord, in an attempt to prevent him working with hacker groups. The order will last for five years. The hack happened while Kurtaj was already under police protection in a Travelodge with his computer confiscated. During his stay, he used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel television to hack Rockstar, Revolut, and Uber. The GTA 6 hack saw him steal 90 clips of an unfinished build well before Rockstar was ready to show gameplay from its anticipated open-world sequel, which launched last week. It resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw dual protagonists Jason and Lucia for the first time. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. It would be over a year before Rockstar finally showed the protagonists itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year. "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code," he said in the company Slack. When the company didn’t respond, he released the files, costing the company $5 million in damages. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? d19339025ff8.title: GTA 6’s Best-Kept Secret Is the Key to Its Whole Design
d19339025ff8.summary: Rockstar kept a reveal in GTA 6's prologue a secret for years, but now we all know it, it's clear how it guides the game's entire design.
d19339025ff8.content: Warning: this story contains spoilers for GTA 6’s prologue and Chapter 1. In the final months of trailers, screenshots, and extended looks leading up to Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s launch, Rockstar was keeping a huge secret. It had revealed Jason and Lucia to the world years before and, by the summer of this year, we knew that their romantic relationship was core to the story. But until the moment the game went live, we had no idea that the pair were parents. As we all found out in the prologue, Jason and Lucia have a son, Tomás. And more than just a baby, this little infant is the key to GTA 6’s entire design ethos. Historically, Rockstar has drawn from classic crime movie tropes to establish the themes of its stories. Tommy Vercetti cut through all in his path on his way to becoming Miami’s premier crime lord. Carl Johnson rallied the boys in the hood on his quest for revenge. And Niko Bellic put his war-honed killing skills to work on the streets of Liberty City. While there are elements of relatability in all these stories – hurt over dead mothers, discovering the lie of the American dream – you’d be in the tiny minority of players if you could claim to truly recognise the lives of GTA’s protagonists as reflections of your own timeline. But things are different this time. As Lucia orders another free water at her local cafe, her RydeMe app notifies her that her driver account has been suspended. With the cost of living rising and the job market increasingly unstable in the real world, Lucia’s reality is just a step away from ours. As a then-single mother with a baby’s life on the line, the thing that pushes her towards serious crime isn’t the lust for power or infinite riches – it’s the simple need for survival. It’s the most relatable and realistic starting point any GTA has delivered. Later in Chapter 1, after being introduced to Mattia and Kat and their extravagant lifestyle, we do see Lucia pine for money in a more classic GTA manner. The lure of the never-ending party is difficult to ignore after nine months behind bars. But the act that put Lucia in jail is key: before holding up the store, she ejects every bullet from her magazine and clears the pistol’s chamber. She has no intention of murder. All she wants is to afford rent and feed her baby. Similarly, Jason is far from the hardened gangster that we’ve historically seen in GTA. While he’s more involved in the criminal scene than Lucia, for him it’s just a job. Staying away from regular employment because of his awkward military history, he finds cash-in-hand wages via Brian’s drug-running operations. While there are sparks every now and again, it’s a low-level job – practically an Amazon driver for a middleman. This helps ground Jason in a more familiar reality; he’s just looking for a simple life, emphasised by GTA 6’s encouraged morning routine of shower, coffee, and a workout. As the innocent emotional stake of the entire piece, Tomás encourages a more realistic depiction of our two protagonists. Tomás is emblematic of all this. As the innocent emotional stake of the entire piece, he encourages a more realistic depiction of our two protagonists. And that increased realism flows into the gameplay systems, mission design, and open-world opportunities. While it would be foolish to suggest that Tomás was the idea that began GTA 6’s pursuit of incredibly detailed realism, he is the character that makes the design feel complete and authentic, despite barely being a part of the story. Less weird is the link between Tomás and the home improvement missions that have ruffled so many feathers among those who think every GTA game should adhere to a very particular formula. bb20beff33b9.title: GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek Reportedly Releases .exe File for Xbox Build, Sparking Concern an Unofficial PC Port Could Be Around the Corner
bb20beff33b9.summary: Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6, sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner.
bb20beff33b9.content: Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 , sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner. The infamous hacker had vowed to release the .exe for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build whether the Cyberleek memecoin hit its market cap target or not , and now it is out in the wild, some within the homebrew scene are preparing to take a close look at it. Cyberleek released the exe with a fresh statement insisting their actions on GTA 6 so far were about “fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry.” Cyberleek also taunts Rockstar parent company Take-Two’s so-far unsuccessful effort to prevent further leaks or, it seems, track down those responsible, saying: “Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving.” They also pushed back on claims the GTA 6 leaks are about little more than pushing a crypto scheme, insisting that crypto was used to generate funds for a secret project outside of the game. “There is no other way to move funds without names,” Cyberleek said, “and this work requires no names.” Some are now predicting that AI-assisted recompilation of the leaked Xbox build could result in GTA 6 on PC in just days, with performance improvements over the console version in weeks. This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay. The release of the Xbox build from this month runs counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released in the summer, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch. Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000. IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats. In the wake of Cyberleek’s initial leaks, Take-Two issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of its search for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, any potential build of the game it was taken from, or this latest Xbox build, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

525ba0d2fc75.title: Family-Friendly Fortnite Streamer Goes Viral After Picking Up GTA 6 And Performing the Ultimate Heelturn, Including a Bloody Zoo Rampage
525ba0d2fc75.summary: Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit.
525ba0d2fc75.content: Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit. For almost a decade, cheery Canadian streamer Nicholas " Nick Eh 30 " Amyoony has amassed a community of millions around his family-friendly Fortnite streams. His personal brand is based on pushing positivity, he's known for never swearing on camera, and he's become one of the few Twitch stars partnered with Epic Games to get a skin of himself made available in-game. So it has, understandably, come as something of a surprise to see wholesome Nick Eh 30 embracing the most dastardly deeds GTA 6 has on offer: kicking pet dogs to death in the street , shooting animals in the zoo , and walking down the length of a train executing every passenger at point blank range . As someone who has followed Nick Eh 30 for a while, seeing him wandering around GTA 6's world eliminating swathes of its animal population while chuckling to himself is indeed odd to see. Social media is awash with similar reactions, with posts from his followers stating things like: "IN WHAT UNIVERSE DO YOU NEED TO BE DOING THIS" and "Years of building ramps in Fortnite could not prepare chat for this." But this is all clearly intentional, down to his streams being labelled as humorously promising "family friendly GTA" gameplay (I'm not sure there's any such thing). And the fact this has led people to actually discuss his streams and share clips further has only proven why he's likely doing this. NickEh30 takes a taser to the Zoo in GTA VI https://t.co/4SAVgUCjYm — yoxic (@yoxics) November 22, 2026 All of that said, it's still a surprise to see Nick squarely aiming for the game's brutal "Irredeemable" criminal profile rating — a label that Rockstar has actually made quite difficult to achieve unless you really, really want to play the game as bloodily as possible. e62602da3146.title: The Definitive Proof That GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption Share The Same Universe
e62602da3146.summary: Here are the seven easter eggs in GTA 6 that prove Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto take place in the same universe.
e62602da3146.content: From action movies to popular memes, there are dozens and dozens of Easter eggs and references to wider pop culture in GTA 6. But Rockstar has also slipped in more than a few nods to some of the studio’s previous games within Leonida. There’s a Manhunt-themed tattoo, for example, and a ludicrously convoluted secret that has already been unearthed involving a portal back to the days of Vice City. But one series is showing up more than others: Red Dead Redemption. We’re still working our way through finding all of them, as is the rest of the internet, but so far we’ve found seven secrets that relate to the developer’s beloved Western games. From hats and guns to road names and license plates, here are seven Red Dead Easter eggs in GTA 6. Valentine Drive If you’re looking for hidden details about Red Dead, the Western-themed Frontier Mini Golf course is a natural place to start. While none of the holes directly tell the tale of Red Dead Revolver, Red Dead Redemption, or its prequel—aside from squinting at hole four and seeing a snowy train wreck as a tangential nod to RDR2’s prologue—there are still things to find. We’ll get on to who can be seen roaming it in a moment, but before you even set foot inside, an Easter egg can be found. That’s because the attraction itself is located on Valentine Drive, a reference to the first major town you explore in Chapter 1 of Red Dead Redemption 2’s story. This is the location where Arthur famously drinks a few too many beers, has a bit of a dance, and looks for his friend, Lenny. Sadly, alcohol doesn’t seem to be served at this Mini Golf, although there’s nothing stopping you from bringing your own six-pack in. Tiny Arthur Morgan Once you’re on the course, though, a little friend with a familiar face riding on his back may well walk up to you. A small chihuahua with a cowboy toy, dressed in remarkably similar clothing to what Red Dead Redemption 2 protagonist Arthur Morgan wore in many of the game’s trailers. Feel free to give the little guy a pet, too, and his gun-toting rider will look like he’s giving it a little “yeehaw”. Adorable. Arthur’s Hat Perhaps more life-sized Arthur Morgan Easter eggs are more your thing, though. Well, get yourself over to Port Gellhorn to get your hands on, and head in, one such thing. Follow the trail of signs and balloons to find a resident looking to get rid of any old tat. Hidden amongst it all, though, is a real treasure. No, not the cow-patterned Hawaiian shirt, but something that will make fans of Red Dead Redemption 2’s hearts flutter a little: a genuine cowboy hat. Not just any cowboy, either, but Arthur himself. The dark brown colour, complete with twisted rope around the rim, is unmistakable, and is now Jason or Lucia’s to wear whenever they like. An absolute bargain at $35, too. Duke Arms As if we needed any further proof that the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption stories take place in the same universe, the Duke Arms Company cements this. At any of Leonida’s Ammu-Nation stores, you can find weapons made by the same gun company that produced the Duke 1853 Navy Revolver in Red Dead Online. On the packaging found inside GTA 6’s gun stores, you can also spot 1853 written out in Roman numerals (MDCCCLIII) on the boxes. It just can’t be a coincidence. First, a mention of Blackwater, the port city from Red Dead Redemption and its prequel, where John Marston chooses to build his ranch near to. But there’s also a familiar name to those who chose to fully engage with RDR2’s side activities. Flaco Hernández was an infamous outlaw who you can meet during the 2018 game’s “The Noblest of Men, and a Woman” stranger mission. 9259c0358563.title: Should You Trust Halifax in GTA 6?
9259c0358563.summary: Should you trust Halifax in GTA 6's chapter three mission, Dubious Provenance? We have the answer.
9259c0358563.content: Warning: Spoilers for the Dubious Provenance mission in chapter three of GTA 6 follow. GTA 6 is full of choices, big and small. In fact, the whole way you choose to play the game is a choice, whether that be as an ultraviolet psychopath or a more professional class of criminal. Or if you decide that Jason and Lucia are a couple hopelessly head-over-heels in love, or more platonic partners in crime. Some choices, however, are much more binary, with instant effects tied to them. One of the clearest examples of this is presented to you during a chapter three mission called Dubious Provenance. Should you trust Halifax or not? The answer is twofold: the smart decision is to reject his offer, but the much more fun option is to place your faith in him. Let me explain. Dubious Provenance kicks off by driving all the way to the fancy town of Capri, found in the east of Leonida, and home to the sort of houses Jason and Lucia can only dream of living in at this point in their story. Just by the centre of town is an antiques store where you’re tasked with bringing the mysterious statue that has fallen into your possession to be valued. Halifax, a man with a fairly convincing British accent, overhears your conversation with the shop’s owner, Evelyn, and offers you a deal. While she isn’t interested in the statue, he most definitely is, telling you that he will get it valued for you if you hand it over. Now, despite his smart appearance, all is not what it seems with Halifax, and without spoiling it too much, he’s not exactly the antiques expert he claims to be. The smart, and arguably correct, choice from a story perspective is to reject him. But the much more fun and beneficial option (if you’re a collectibles hunter) is to accept. Accepting adds a couple more main missions to the Dubious Provenance story rather than just ending it there and then. You’ll also receive the Crowex Octane “Bobby Ambrose” unique watch in return. This is a missable collectible otherwise. But more importantly, you get two more very fun missions to play through. The first includes a stealthy infiltration and a massive, and I mean, massive revelation about Halifax. The second is one of the best chase sequences in GTA 6, scored hilariously to a great bit of contrapuntal music. For full spoilers and a step-by-step guide, you can check out our walkthrough . If you reject, you won’t get the watch, but you will have a second shot at playing through these missions. Halifax will later contact you and give you the option to phone him if you change your mind, transforming these main missions into optional ones. These must be completed by the end of chapter three , or they’ll disappear forever, though. Ultimately, the choice to accept or reject comes down to whether you want the watch or not. Of course, you can choose to just never contact him again if you’re desperate to progress through the story as quickly as possible, but you will miss out on a great bit of fun as a result. So, should you trust Halifax during Dubious Provenance? I’d say yes; it’s a much more fun road to take if you’re looking to squeeze every bit of enjoyment out of GTA 6. c77d02ebbf8b.title: Over Half of GTA 6 Watch Time Came From Viewers Under 25 Years Old
c77d02ebbf8b.summary: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.
c77d02ebbf8b.content: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts. After 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally out in the wild. Rockstar’s highly-anticipated release has already broken numerous records, one of the most impressive being that it became the single most popular game ever on both Twitch and Kick just 26 hours after its global release. Now that it’s had a little time to breathe, more data is rolling in, including information about who’s watching streamers play the game. StreamsCharts , a data analytics company that studies games-focused streaming platforms, discovered that most viewers of GTA 6 broadcasts tend to trend under the age of 25. According to Streamlabs’ stats, 30.8% of viewers in GTA 6 streams are 20 - 24 years old, making up the bulk of those watching the game across Kick, Twitch, and YouTube. (Painfully, StreamsCharts pointed out that these players were in elementary school when GTA 5 came out.) 16.8% of these viewers are 17 - 19, with 8.5% accounting for viewers 16 or under. The second-largest age range watching GTA 6 streams are viewers aged 25 - 29. 11.6% of viewers are 30 - 34, and the numbers keep dropping from there. StreamsCharts also found that an overwhelming majority of these viewers are single men, accounting for 83.8% of the gender divide. That’s not to say that gals aren’t also watching streamers play Rockstar’s latest; 14% of viewers are female, and if you’ve been on social media lately, you’ve probably seen a fair few female players showing off their outfits for Jason and Lucia or the viral conversation about how it’s, oddly, comparable to a crime-focused version of The Sims. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the United States makes up the bulk of GTA 6 viewership. Brazil isn’t far behind, coming in at 12.4% of the game’s total audience; Spain and Germany follow at 6.9% and 6.8%, respectively. Certain games have also experienced a drop in viewership following GTA 6’s release. StreamsCharts found that GTA 5 had the sharpest drop-off on Twitch, followed by the platform’s Just Chatting category and World of Warcraft. The GTA hype train is in full swing, and it’s making big bucks for Rockstar. The company reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion from the game in just 24 hours, making it the single biggest entertainment launch in history. Internet provider Comcast even revealed that it experienced its highest-traffic day ever as players downloaded the game to their consoles, and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 was its biggest game launch in the company’s history. cdf8ec2943d6.title: Cyberpunk 2 Is Still a Ways Out, but CD Projekt Red Says Its RPGs Will Come Out Faster in the Future
cdf8ec2943d6.summary: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4, but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.
cdf8ec2943d6.content: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4 , but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle. In a November 24 earnings call , CD Projekt Red VP of Strategy & Investor Relations Karolina Gnaś said the team is "making good progress with Cyberpunk 2, we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production." Although she couldn't provide a clear date when we'll hear more about the game, she did add that the studio plans to have around 200 developers by the end of 2026 and 320 by the end of next year. It is admittedly a bit early to expect any kind of information about the Cyberpunk sequel, but it has been simmering in the background since at least 2022 , and it sounds like CD Projekt Red wants to speed up development of its massive RPGs. In its consolidated earnings report , CD Projekt Red admitted that most of its games "normally take 3 to 6 years to produce," mostly due to working on one game at a time. But that strategy has since changed. In that same report, the company said, "At the moment, the CD Projekt Red studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future." Whether or not that new timeline will affect Cyberpunk 2 is the question. But even if that faster development timeline is in effect for Cyberpunk 2, it's likely we'll still have to wait a while to actually see it in the wild. In an earnings report last year, when Cyberpunk 2 entered pre-production, CD Projekt CEO Michał Nowakowski suggested that CDPR's games take four or five years to move from pre-production to release, which would put the game somewhere in 2030 or 2031. And given that the game still hasn't entered full production, it isn't likely we're going to see some sort of rapid release after the Witcher 4 in 2028. We're probably going to be waiting a little while longer for Cyberpunk 2, but it's already sounding like the game is taking shape. Just last month, associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a lot of the developers working on Cyberpunk 2 are former modders. Sasko went on to claim that "the modding community is really keeping [Cyberpunk 2077] alive," so hopefully that energy translates to Cyberpunk 2 – whenever it comes out.

f43e47a2c2d6.title: 'Crazy Secretive' — GTA 6 Voice Actor Reveals Details of Rockstar's 'Humongous' NDA
f43e47a2c2d6.summary: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
f43e47a2c2d6.content: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.” Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America. In a November 20 interview with Page Six , Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle. “Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said. She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind. “In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it. And after that, I don’t know — whatever was in front of my face disappeared. “ Lopez revealed that she wasn’t told what the project was for, but figured it out based on context clues from an email titled “heard by millions,” saying she “read it and knew what it was for.” She also didn’t know that Bad Bunny would be co-hosting the Cocoteo station alongside her, leading to a wild realization once Rockstar released the radio stations before the game actually came out. “We knew nothing. I saw the liners, and when I saw the liners I was like, ‘Okay, I know why I got the gig.’ ‘Cause it was like Puerto Rican dot com. It was super easy. But it was so cool, because Rockstar let me be myself. …they were like, ‘Issa, we want natural. Whatever you got, we want,'" she said. The actors in GTA 6 were extremely secretive about their involvement in the project. Most notably, actress Manni L. Perez, who plays Lucia, was under immense pressure after fans sleuthed her social media accounts and figured out it was her before she could officially reveal the information. Now, she’s up for best performance at The Game Awards, which is one of eight nominations the game has secured mere weeks before the show takes place this December. Other performers who have finally revealed their involvement in the game are Mandy’s actress, Lexie Shoaibi , as well as the voice and performance artist for Jason Duval, Dylan Rourke . Rockstar released the full credits for the game, too, which you can check out here — just beware of spoilers if you haven’t finished it yet. a1633ea34175.title: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
a1633ea34175.summary: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
a1633ea34175.content: Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6 . GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements. Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem. However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime. "Best thing about that early chapter is just how low stakes and casual it feels," said X user @CS11__ after spending 41 hours in Chapter 1 alone. "I forced myself not to go farther than Hamlet, so I really only ever experienced these two small areas in 40 hours. [...] The game hardly opened up, but it still felt unbelievably rich and fun." But... what is it these people are actually doing, if not blowing stuff up and creating tons of chaos? Some fans were just going through the motions, giving themselves daily routines that involved working out, taking on relaxing hobbies, and exploring. "[A] lot of roleplaying, day-to-day living type stuff," said Aaron Espionza on X , who estimated that he spent around 15–18 hours before picking up Lucia from prison. "I had a routine even when I would wake up, drive to the juice bar down the street, get my orange juice, and then say hello to the locals. If anyone said anything mean, I would get violent and throw empty juice cups at them. [I] did the workout routines. Basketball was a favorite of mine. Side stuff with Cal fishing, Donnie pick-ups, and scuba. But so much of it was testing how much detail Rockstar put into it. 'If I do this , will they do that ?' type of systems exploration. Always came away surprised." X user @scaasm noted that the lower stakes nature of Chapter 1 even prompted him to follow traffic laws and use manual turn signals in GTA 6: "I follow traffic laws unless I'm doing something criminal, and generally just taking it very slow. [I'm] loving every moment." The location itself was also a big driving point for a lot of fans, some of whom have personal connections or apprecation for its real life counterpart: "As someone from Florida, I think the Keys is one of those locations that they absolutely nailed (waning sands outlets too; they look exactly like the Orlando ones)," said @piterparker69 on X . "It felt kinda uncanny driving around (especially the 7 Mile Bridge) because of how good it replicates real life." b396533c7816.title: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
b396533c7816.summary: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
b396533c7816.content: The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version. In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed. Australia’s classification laws allow illicit drug use in games, but using them can’t provide the player with gameplay benefits. Overpowering your stamina (and everything else) is still possible via the use of adrenaline in the Australian version of GTA 6, and it’s also still possible to drink and smoke whenever you want. The general use of cocaine in story moments also still remains in the Australian version of GTA 6, because these instances aren’t associated with any in-game buffs. While the caveat that forbids rewards for illicit drug use is bespoke to Australia – and doesn’t apply to NZ – NZ’s rating system (which does piggyback on some Australian and UK classification decisions for unrestricted content ) has its own idiosyncrasies. These recently caught out IllFonic’s recent Halloween multiplayer game , which was refused classification in Australia for illicit drug use linked to an incentive or reward (that is, that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player). Halloween since made its way to NZ, but not Australia. Since this is not Rockstar’s first rodeo, it knew exactly the tweak GTA 6 would require to skirt this continuing quirk in Australian video game ratings and avoid multiple submissions. d85018864848.title: GTA 6 Analysis Shows PS5 Version Suffers 'Substantially' More Frequent Frame Rate Drops Than Xbox Series X Version, Sparking Debate About Sony's 'Plays Best on PS5' Marketing
d85018864848.summary: The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6, and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.
d85018864848.content: The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6 , and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5. Sony’s high-profile marketing deal for GTA 6 involved the key phrase, “Plays Best on PS5,” and while that marketing tagline encompasses more than just performance, many are now questioning its validity with GTA 6 out in the wild. Digital Foundry found that Xbox Series X provides a “virtually identical visual presentation” to the PS5 in terms of overall image clarity and presentation quality, but there is a significant split on performance. As Rockstar had announced before launch, GTA 6 “targets” 30 frames per second across all platforms, from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, but there are moments where the frame rate drops. According to DF’s analysis , the frame rate suffers more on PS5 than Series X. Here's what DF said on the issue: PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off. Of course, the PS5 Pro version offers the best experience in terms of performance, but it’s interesting to see the Xbox Series X outperform the PS5 here. Some are pointing to non-performance related features, such as the PS5’s haptic feedback, which is great for driving, as playing a role in the phrase “Plays Best on PS5,” and we should be used to marketing speak that is technically not wrong by now. But, as DF reveals, when it comes to performance, there can be no doubting the clear winner. Indeed, some are calling the “Plays Best on PS5,” phrase “grossly misleading,” claiming that Sony should have said “Plays Best on PS5 Pro” instead. “I’ve been f***ing fooled,” one person said in the comments of DF’s YouTube video . “They did kind of say in the fine print that ‘best’ referred to the features in the DualSense controller,” another person countered. “If you are advertising ‘Plays best on X’ to gamers, the immediate thought is going to be ‘Out the two places I can play the game, it is going to play the best on the X console,’” another suggested. “What does ‘Play’ mean to that audience? Performance, stability, possibly higher resolution, less texture pop-in.” In June, when Sony trumpeted the “Plays Best on PS5” marketing line , it highlighted how GTA 6 takes advantage of the PS5 DualSense controller's haptic feedback and integrated speaker. Sony also highlighted its Tempest 3D AudioTech, which allows you to "surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida" through its "highly accurate audio positioning." GTA 6 would also "leverage the PS5's ultra-high speed SSD" to experience GTA 6 "with near-instant load times." Sony's blog post made no mention of performance. Meanwhile, there are questions around GTA 6’s use of FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series S version of the game only . Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, which makes GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox. It’s thought this tech is what made GTA 6 possible at 30fps on the underpowered Series S in the first place. Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game instead use Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro uses Sony’s PSSR upscaler. But why not use FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 also? Similarly, if the PS5 version already supports PSSR, why not use Sony’s AI upscaling model QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution)? Elsewhere, fans are just marveling at the performance of GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, which — as we’ve reported — shows what Microsoft’s cheaper console is capable of. edec9b59fe82.title: Take-Two Appears to Be Trying to Scrub GTA 6 PC Ports From the Internet, as Vibecoders Race Toward Controversial World First
edec9b59fe82.summary: Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
edec9b59fe82.content: Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game. This week, Cyberleek allegedly released the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior, sparking a race within the homebrew scene to port the build to PC. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. But it looks like Take-Two is taking action, reportedly convincing GitHub to delete an entire network of 3,007 repositories via a DMCA takedown notice. The takedown we know about relates to ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the over 2,900 forks attached to it, which Take-Two said facilitated copyright infringement of GTA 6. Take-Two alleged that the repository Project Leonida repository "exceeds the license Rockstar Games grants to users, constituting copyright infringement.” Here, Take-Two claimed that the repository violated at least Section 2.3 of Rockstar Games’ terms of service: "The limited license granted in this Agreement does not give you any right to, and you may not, sell, copy, loan, lease, distribute, disassemble, decompile, decrypt, hack, derive source code from, reverse engineer, modify, create derivative works, commercialize, or otherwise exploit the Services (including the Content), Virtual Items, or your Account unless subject to separate, express written terms provided by Rockstar permitting such conduct.” Additionally, there’s an interesting note in the takedown order that addresses the “bring your own files” defence we’ve seen so often from the homebrew community when it comes to unofficial ports of video games. As you’d expect, Take-Two isn’t in favor of it, insisting that in this case, the files the user must provide come from the unauthorized GTA 6 Xbox build Cyberleek leaked online. IGN has asked Take-Two for comment. According to now deleted social media posts, NotRexed, author of the Leonida project, shut it down entirely. There are also screenshots of its Discord showing users posting disclaimers distancing themselves from Project Leonida in case of a federal investigation. However, many similar projects remain active, risking similar action from Take-Two. Seemingly undeterred, these projects are ongoing, with some getting close to creating a PC port of GTA 6 that is somewhat playable. Some are even streaming their efforts, showing how they are vibecoding a port using agent prompts such as "make no mistakes," "keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," and "work faster." This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay. As you've probably seen from various viral clips on social media, people are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. Kevin, the creator of the port, posted a farewell message to the unofficial port’s website . “GTA V has always been one of my favorite games,” he said. “I've made mods for it, worked with FiveM, managed and hosted FiveM servers, and played on plenty of others. It has given me a lot of great memories. Getting to bring it to people who don't have a PC or a console, so they could play it on a phone, has been really, really cool. I honestly never thought this game could run on a phone at all. “Take-Two Interactive, through their lawyers, has sent me a cease and desist asking me to stop all activity under the Five Star Port name and everything related to it. I am complying with it.” Five Star Port’s website, app, and online services were shut down immediately. The Telegram and Discord groups have been made read-only and will be deleted on November 27. “I'm not involved in and don't endorse any continuation, rebrand or copy of the port, and I can't help with files or links,” Kevin added. He also posted a warning that scammers have been passing around copies of the port, claiming to have a “new version” of it. These could spread computer viruses. “Thank you again to everyone who supported this project: everyone who playtested, everyone who sent suggestions and feedback, and everyone who helped make it a great port that is actually fully playable on an iPhone,” Kevin signed off. “That still feels wild to me.” Take-Two has a history of forcing fan projects offline, so perhaps it comes as no surprise to see Five Star Port fall by the wayside. The company is currently battling homebrew efforts to vibecode a PC port of GTA 6 , which some believe is mere days away from being playable. ba4486d24f5e.title: The Witcher 3 and Assassin's Creed 'Reset Player Expectations' for Open-World Action RPGs, So the Fable Reboot Devs Had to Look Beyond the Original Trilogy for Inspiration
ba4486d24f5e.summary: Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.
ba4486d24f5e.content: Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade. Work on Fable reportedly started in 2016, and only now, 10 years later, is it near release. It’s suffered a tumultuous development but, unlike some other costly Microsoft gaming projects, it has avoided closure amid sweeping layoffs and restructuring at Xbox. In a new interview with GamesIndustry.biz , Playground Games co-founder and Fable general manager Ralph Fulton touched on the trials and tribulations Fable has endured over the years. Playground set up a new team to make Fable in addition to its hugely popular racing game franchise, Forza Horizon, and set out to make a game in a genre it had no prior experience with. And Fable is a big role-playing game, with all the bells and whistles you'd expect. So, Fable isn’t technically a debut game from Playground, but it sort of is. In terms of what’s changed, Fulton said that technology had “advanced” during development, pointing to a reset of player expectations with the release of CD Projekt’s fantasy RPG masterpiece The Witcher 3 and then Assassin’s Creed’s move towards the RPG genre. This, Fulton explained, meant that Playground had to look beyond the original Fable trilogy for inspiration to ensure it created a reboot that would meet modern open-world standards. “In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard,” Fulton explained. “And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG. “All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.” Despite this, the scope of Fable actually decreased over time, with the project starting with “an enormous potential scope.” In August, Playground confirmed that Fable’s main quest will take around 20 hours to beat , with an additional 15-20 hours of side and open-world exploration content available. Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12-and-a-half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours , and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13-and-a-half hours . So, the Fable reboot is shaping up to be the longest in the series. Fable is set for launch on February 23, 2027, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.

9fc248884698.title: GTA 6: Breaking Down The Cleanest Bank Robbery We've Seen So Far
9fc248884698.summary: One GTA 6 player has robbed $160,000 in just one minute in the cleanest bank robbery we’ve seen yet. Here's how they did it.
9fc248884698.content: Warning: This article talks about gameplay mechanics from chapter four of GTA 6, but contains no story spoilers. GTA 6 is a game all about making money. One of the quickest and most profitable ways of doing that is by robbing one of Vice City’s biggest banks. It’s also one of the riskiest, though; we’ve a legion of law enforcement destined to descend upon you once that alarm is triggered. That doesn’t mean a clean escape isn’t possible, though, and that’s just what one streamer has showcased, in perhaps the most impressive manner we’ve seen so far. Video game streamer Sway set about his mission to the downtown Lombank for all its worth via a popular method – tailing a security van. These are the green and white vans you sometimes see driving around the map, which, if you follow for long enough, will lead you to a bank where the vault will be left wide open for you to enter. You can also make the locations of these trucks visible by paying Yasmani a hefty $10,000 tip for the info. It’s worth noting that this option isn’t available until chapter four, with banks not being able to be successfully robbed at all until partway through GTA 6’s third chapter, once you gain the ability to cash in on marked bills. Otherwise, you’ll end up as Lucia can in the prologue, with a whole load of coloured dye all over you. Anyway, back to Sway’s attempted heist, and just because the security guard has opened the vault doesn’t mean you can simply walk in and out of the building carrying a load of cash. There are numerous options you can take, including blasting your way in and getting in and out as quickly and violently as possible, or entering through the back rooms to sneak past everyone. The latter is the way that Sway mostly went with. First, he shot out a security camera in the rear alley with a silenced pistol, before cracking open a garage door and quickly knocking out a guard with a quick pistol whip. Another couple of security members fell unconscious thanks to the blunt end of a gun as he made his way swiftly into the vault. Just noting the excellent choice of “old person” mask from Jason here, too. Cleanest Bank Robbery you'll see in GTA 6. $150k in 1 minute. simple and clean. https://t.co/Y8GqDuydvd — sway (@swaywtw) November 25, 2026 Next come the stacks of marked bills, which are hurriedly bundled into stash bags by Lucia. This action triggers the bank’s alarm systems, and always will, as far as I know. The cloud-based security camera system can’t be overrun and will always alert the cops once a couple of bundles of notes hit the bottom of your bag. With $122,000 already secured, he smartly swaps to controlling Jason, who can fill up his own bag to maximise the profits. With the grand total now sitting at $160,000, the hard part begins. At least, in theory, it should be difficult. This clearly isn’t Sway’s first run, though, as he doesn’t panic at all. He runs back to where he entered from, kneecapping an onrushing guard with a single bullet before reopening the garage door to exit the bank and remove the couple’s masks, in turn removing the appearance marker from the top right. Cleverly, Lucia’s personal vehicle — a sleek sports car, yet another sign this isn’t his first heist if he can afford to register that — is sitting just feet away. He changes into a fresh pair of clothes, holsters his weapon, and just like that, becomes completely incognito. Little do the cops who have just rolled up know that the people walking past them are exactly who they’re at the bank for, and he simply walks across the road and out of the red circle on the minimap towards freedom. It’s an incredibly quick, clean in-and-out operation, and the sort of robbery that feels extra satisfying to pull off in GTA 6. It’s the kind of hidden-in-plain-sight thrill that you’d expect from the likes of the Hitman series, but pulled off in a dynamic open world that loves to throw surprises your way. 5ae7689400b1.title: This GTA 6 Radio Station Represents Its Florida-Inspired Setting Perfectly
5ae7689400b1.summary: Southern hip-hop deserves its respect in rap history and GTA 6 celebrates it with its own radio station full of bangers from Outkast, T.I., Trick Daddy, Gucci Mane, and so many more.
5ae7689400b1.content: Radio stations have always been a staple of Grand Theft Auto, filled with licensed (and some original) songs alongside crazy-ass talk shows. GTA 6 is unprecedented in this field, with its massive tracklist and over-the-top on-air personalities. But we all have the music genres we gravitate towards when picking out a station, and the one I'm rarely ever changing is Dirty South Classics – basically a playlist of the Southern hip-hop bangers I grew up listening to. It's also a thematic fit for GTA 6's setting of Leonida, an obvious parallel to the state of Florida. While you traditionally wouldn't consider South Florida or the city of Miami part of the American South, the rest of Florida is largely culturally aligned with the region's states like Georgia, Mississippi, and parts of Texas (namely Houston). These are key distinctions to make in the context of music, especially what we consider Southern hip-hop – colloquially known as 'dirty south' hip-hop, hence the station name. Deep bass, rattling hi-hats, catchy melodies with instrumentals that either align with aggressive trap beats or the more soulful funk; characteristics of the genre that you hear throughout Dirty South Classics. Because of its importance as a subgenre, and as a prominent cultural touchstone of the region that GTA 6 is trying to portray, it got its own dedicated station separate from VCRR, which is for more contemporary rap hits. So, admittedly, Dirty South Classics laser-targets uncs who scrapped in the schoolyard in the early/mid 2000s. Hell, the station is hosted by Trick Daddy and Trina, two major figures in the Southern rap game from Miami (with interstitials from Gucci Mane himself). Just in the first few hours of my playthrough of GTA 6, I kept thinking to myself, 'They put this song in the game?!' And they all took me back to a very specific time and place as I rapped along off the top of the brain like I was a youngin' all over again. I'm glad GTA 6 went with Outkast's "Player's Ball" instead of the Atlanta-based duo's more well-known hits. It has the quintessential sound of a classic Southern hip-hop track with a bold bassline and funky instrumentals rounded out with Andre 3000's falsetto hook. This particular style can be heard throughout their debut album "Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik" (1994) – although Outkast's sound changed in interesting ways afterward and exploded in popularity, it's still my favorite record of theirs. Knuck If You Buck's first four notes activate any 30-something-year-old who had to square up and run the fade at school in a moment's notice. On the other end of the genre spectrum, I can’t believe I'm hearing Dem Franchize Boyz' "White Tee" in a game in the year 2026. It was their first song to break containment in 2004 and it's an ode to, well, the universality of the plain white t-shirt – affordable, easy to match in any outfit, and helpful in keeping a low profile, as covered in the song's lyrics. This especially resonated in the era of tall tees in my neighborhood, but I still don't understand the hostility toward throwbacks. Maybe I shouldn't have been listening to them when I was a kid, but Three 6 Mafia's "Side 2 Side" was my favorite song from the Memphis-based trio. That dark, melancholic cello melody that runs throughout the track is undeniably catchy and Juicy J's flow on the last verse goes so hard. I'm a little surprised GTA 6 didn't go with the more popular remix featuring Bow Wow, but I am glad because the original version here is damn near perfect. Lastly, I have to shout out "Knuck If You Buck" by Crime Mob and Lil Scrappy , the universal fight or flight mode anthem. Its dark, aggressive sound and trunk-knocking bass makes you feel invincible, and those first four notes activate any 30-something-year-old who had to square up and run the fade at school in a moment's notice. I'm scratching the surface of the Dirty South Classics radio station, only four of the 39 songs which include hits from Big Tymers, T.I.

e614da20d17c.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
e614da20d17c.summary: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
e614da20d17c.content: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar. When speaking with Kotaku , Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6 . According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story. “Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.” The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that. GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games. However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? 59446fc27a7b.title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
59446fc27a7b.summary: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
59446fc27a7b.content: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game. If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects. This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3 .) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother. Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations. “FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote . “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…” That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.” “Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied. GTA 6 is a game like no other. 9675ea516879.title: Another Modder Uses AI to Make a Multiplayer Mode for The Last of Us Part 2 — Will Sony Shut This One Down, Too?
9675ea516879.summary: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2, insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."
9675ea516879.content: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2 , insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down." The Last of Us had a brilliant multiplayer mode, with tense gunfights powered by weapon sway, smart cover, and nail-biting in-round crafting that forced you to dig around in your backpack as bullets whizzed over your bonce. That’s why so many people were excited when Naughty Dog announced a Factions multiplayer game in the works based on The Last of Us Part 2 . Naughty Dog, however, eventually realized that making a live-service game would change the studio forever, and cancelled the project to focus instead on its upcoming sci-fi game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet . The Last of Us Part 2 made some brilliant tweaks to the combat, allowing for better mobility and deeper stealth. The feel of the weapons, the crunch of the impacts, the audiovisual spectacle of it all was just something else, but we can only experience it in single-player, officially. It’s no wonder people want to make Factions happen, even without Sony’s approval. And in September, a promising mod made some big strides towards getting multiplayer working in The Last of Us Part 2. As soon as it started to get traction, however, the mod was sent a cease and desist letter from Sony . “Hey everyone, as you all know, the TLOU 2 Multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month,” wrote creator 'Speclizer' at the time. “Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you’ll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own.” Now there’s a new mod hoping to avoid the eye of Sauron, and it’s already out. The mod is called Twelve Weeks and was built specifically for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC, using, its creator has admitted, generative AI. Modder 'Kellie' admitted to using Claude code for most of the game's development, and AI was even used to write the lore dumps you can find in the game. The art was, however, made using Blender . The Last of Us returns with a new online multiplayer mode called TWELVE WEEKS created for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC. This free mod is a work in progress allowing players to experience a new version of the beloved Factions multiplayer with tactical survival gameplay https://t.co/2P8Wv4abQb — 𝗩𝗢𝗬𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗘 (@VoyagersRevenge) November 24, 2026 It features reworked levels — Supply Raid and Interrogation for now — with team-based 4v4 combat, new weapons, and character customization. Players can use gadgets like molotovs and smoke bombs, while fighting against other players as the WLF and Seraphites. The mod even adds brutal execution moves. You can grab Twelve Weeks on Nexus Mods . However, the mod probably won't last long. The modders have attempted to cover their backs with a repository disclaimer that said: "Twelve Weeks is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog. The Last of Us is a trademark of its owners. You need your own legitimately purchased copy of the game (Steam). This repository contains no game files and no assets taken from the game." Will Sony take action? In a reply to someone on YouTube , Kellie said the previous Factions mod got hit by Sony because it was paywalled. "Mine is released already for free and in open source," they said. "Since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down." While The Last of Us Online was canceled, there are hints that Naughty Dog may be ready to return to the series for The Last of Us 3 . And then there is HBO's The Last of Us TV series , which is currently shooting its third (and likely last) season.

7a9dee8803fe.title: GTA 6 Weather Still Not Varied Even After the Patch? PS5 Players Are Sharing a Method That May Help Rain and Thunderstorms Kick In
7a9dee8803fe.summary: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
7a9dee8803fe.content: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically. Lack of weather variety was something I noticed myself during the game’s review period, but Rockstar deployed a small fix during that time too. It was hard to tell whether it was working as intended because the weather also grows more stark as you move through the game. “The weather types change throughout each day, and the overall weather pattern changes per chapter, evolving from generally very good weather in the first chapter to much more changeable and stormy in the last chapter,” said Owen Shepherd, vice president of art: lighting and rendering at Rockstar, when I asked. “This is analogous to Florida’s weather patterns in winter through to summer autumn. During the first chapters there are pockets of rain but due to the localization of weather it is possible to miss these." However, it seems like the issue persisted into the live version of the game, blurring the line between thematically appropriate and accurate weather patterns and unintended bug. The latest patch fixed this for the most part, but some players found they were still experiencing minimal weather changes. If you’re having the same issue, there might be a fix (discovered by X / Twitter user @mauricioce85796 ). On PS5, you need to turn off your console and boot it into safe mode by holding the power button down until it beeps. From there, choose option six and select “clear system cache.” According to people who have tested it, this forces the patch to do its job. “I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather,” said Rockstar fan account Gameroll . “I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted.” Of course, this could be a placebo, but players in the replies have been trying it and immediately seeing results. “Guys, I can confirm, it’s working,” said one happy X / Twitter user who showcased a rainy clip. “Can confirm, weather is more varied!” said another . Clearing your cache on PS5 won’t delete game saves or installed games. It just deletes temporary system files and lets the console recreate fresh ones without erasing your games, saved data, screenshots, or account settings. It helps resolve system feature glitches, slow performance, stuttering, app or game launch errors, and network or sync hiccups. People have been doing it for years, claiming to see performance benefits as a result. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? 6f2332e9a001.title: GTA 6's Cartel Heist Might Be Rockstar's Best Ever Mission, But Only If You Do It Badly
6f2332e9a001.summary: GTA 6's chapter three heist might be Rockstar's best ever mission, but only if you do it badly.
6f2332e9a001.content: Warning: This article contains spoilers for chapter three of GTA 6. Chapter 3 of GTA 6 ends with a bang. It’s arguably Rockstar’s greatest ever mission and a culmination of every bank job the developer has designed since GTA 4’s Three Leaf Clover burst onto the scene. A daring raid on the Sinfrontera National Bank in downtown Vice City, what starts out as a slick operation quickly goes haywire, resulting in shootouts with armored police, helicopters chasing a bus that has had the roof ripped off, and the death of one of your gang members. The funny thing is, you may be reading that and thinking that’s not what happened to you at all. That’s because the back half of The Cartel Heist can go in wildly different directions. You can do it much more cleanly, but it’s nowhere near as fun. Sorry, Nicole. A lot has to go in your favour to execute the perfect heist. Making sure you correctly prep is key, meaning you’ll have to extract all of the info possible out of Monty when he’s dangling over reptilian teeth, protect Pete’s shipment of weapons correctly, and plant enough explosives on the cell towers. Then there’s also everything you have to get going your way inside the mission itself, which is mainly tied to not wasting time and nailing the vault minigame. You can get the full details on everything you’ll need to do, step-by-step, on our excellent guides page . Nail it, and your getaway driver will turn up as planned by the underground entrance; you’ll load up the truck with stacks of cash and simply drive off undetected. There are obvious benefits to doing this. Not only is there the satisfaction of pulling off such a complex job cleanly, but you’ll earn $150,000 from it, rather than the $100,000 you’d otherwise get, plus Nicole, your charming safecracking tutor, will survive. What you will miss out on, though, is one of Rockstar’s finest blockbuster sequences. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008. The path truly branches once you leave the bank’s vault, but in all truth, your fate has likely been long sealed by that point. You’ll have needed to keep a keen eye on your time in the bottom right corner and have made sure all ten bundles of bills have been secured by the time the alarm goes off and all hell breaks loose. That’s when things kick up a notch, and legions of Vice City police and NOOSE enforcers turn up at the front doors. A lobby shootout commences, with enemies turning up from all directions in an effort to stop you from leaving with your haul. It's a fantastic encounter that borders on sensory overload thanks to the rattle of gunfire, thick smoke, and blaring alarms. The slick transitions between characters only add to the sense of cinema, with Lucia throwing a smoke grenade launcher up to the balcony for Jason to catch, punctuated by a highly satisfying second or two of slow motion. This elegantly moves the action onto the streets, allowing you to get a glimpse of the full challenge awaiting you and your gang outside. Michael Mann’s Heat has long been an influence on Grand Theft Auto, but never has the sensation of watching the movie’s signature heist been replicated as well as it has here. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008. As the fight moves outdoors, Raul’s backup plan comes to fruition with Karim arriving behind the wheel of a public bus. It’s not until now, though, that we get to see him in full flow, leading with calm authority. He’s quickly become one of my favourite characters across the whole Grand Theft Auto series — embodying the swagger and ruthless execution of a lusciously long-maned Danny Ocean. 592086181c5d.title: Watching TV in GTA 6 Is More Depressing Than Fun, Except for One Show
592086181c5d.summary: GTA 6's TV content is impressive on a technical level, but apart from one standout show, it's not all that fun to actually watch.
592086181c5d.content: It seems there’s almost nothing you can’t do in Grand Theft Auto VI, other than solicit prostitutes . Far more than just being a murder and crime spree simulator, the game allows you to kick back and do everything from play basketball to remodel your house to work out at the gym. And yes, that long list of side activities includes watching television. GTA 6 includes multiple channels of original programming , featuring everything from breaking Vice City news reports to Adult Swim-style animated sitcoms to cheesy telenovelas. As with so much about the new game, the level of detail Rockstar undertook here is impressive. But despite all that, I found that actually sitting down to watch TV in-game wasn’t quite the entertaining experience I was hoping for. If anything, it was a little depressing. Weazel News: Satire or Sad Reality? To recap, there are three live TV channels in GTA 6 - the Fox News-spoofing Weazel News, the Telemundo parody Megamundo, and the travel-focused Visit Leonida. For the purposes of this piece, I’m mostly focusing on the former channel. Megamundo is a fun sendup of traditional Spanish-language soap operas, but not having any real attachment to that genre, it’s a joke that only has so much mileage for me. And Visit Leonida is definitely the most limited of the three channels. This stream cycles through various breaking news reports, a mockumentary-style series called “The Tyrone Show,” and several different animated sitcoms. And commercials. Dozens and dozens of satirical commercials for all sorts of in-universe products and services. Initially, you can’t help but sit back and admire the sheer effort that went into making all this content. The TV channels are a very minor feature in the game, and I’m sure many people won’t even really pay attention to them amid all the other countless side activities. The simple fact that you can spend literal hours just sitting in front of a fake TV and not really see any repeat content is impressive. But once the initial novelty wears off, watching TV isn’t what I’d describe as one of the more rewarding pastimes in GTA 6. Weazel News actually left me feeling a bit stressed out and unhappy after a while. It was hard to put my finger on it at first, but I think what it comes down to is that the political and social satire hits a little too close to home. For a Scottish-based studio, Rockstar North is generally pretty adept at satirizing American culture with these games - whether it’s remixing the best elements of classic crime films or lampooning the average American’s love of fast food, beer, and guns. You get a heaping helping of all of that with Weazel TV, particularly in the many faux-commercials where colorful characters hawk various brands of alcohol or campaign for a missile launcher in every home or what have you. The problem is that this material no longer feels as outlandish as it once might have. The sad truth is that real life in the US moved beyond parody at some point in the last 10-15 years. It’s something that a lot of sources of satire have dealt with lately, from South Park to The Onion. How do you top reality when reality has become so unhinged and unbelievable? GTA’s TV content is in the same boat. A lot of it doesn’t feel particularly far removed from reality anymore. Between extreme right-wing news channels and the digital hellscape that is social media, there’s a real cultural brain rot that’s taken hold. 1bc582e3cba2.content: Warning! Potential spoilers for GTA 6 follow. Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open (check out IGN's guide to all ATM locations in GTA 6 if you need help finding one). First, though, you need to be able to deal with marked bills through a fence called Yasmini, otherwise the money inside the ATM is worthless and a dye pack will explode in your face. When I got to snatching ATMs, I thought it was cool, but the juice didn’t seem worth the squeeze. It’s kinda hard to keep things on the downlow when you’re backing a truck up to an ATM, ripping it out of a wall, and tearing down the street with the thing still attached, hoping it’ll burst open and spill its contents onto the street. And when it finally does break open, you have to shoot the money drawers open to get to the goods inside — all for a payout between $6,000-$10,000. It wasn’t worth the effort, honestly. But there’s a new trick players have discovered to crack those eggs immediately and move onto the next before the cops even know you’re there. I’ve tried it, and like Todd Howard famously once said: it just works. How to quickly steal an ATM in GTA 6 Here’s what you do. First, you need a truck or other heavy vehicle with a winch attachment at the back. You reverse up to the ATM like normal, and the winch connects to the machine. Now drive forward until the line is taut. From there, get out of your vehicle and walk up to the ATM with a C4 charge. Hold down aim, and a prompt to place it on the ATM should show up, allowing you to set it on the front with Circle/B. Or throw it at the front of the machine — whatever works. Once it’s in place, you want to get back in your car and accelerate hard. When it pulls out of the wall, keep dragging it but immediately press unhook, followed by the same button to detonate your charge. It’s important these two actions happen immediately after each other, because the ATM needs to be moving when the explosion happens or the drawers can stay inside the machine. Done correctly, you can walk over and scoop up the cash and escape before the cops even arrive at the scene. They’ll still be figuring out what happened while you’re hooking up to the next machine, pulling, and sparking up a Cuban. If you need more C4, there’s a free stash of the stuff in the back of Yasmani’s. You can also top up at any Ammunation. This, though, I can get onboard with because it’s just playing the game as intended in an efficient way, and it’s great fun to slip in and out without the cops getting a whiff of you.
