IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games. There comes a time in every professional criminal’s life when you’ve got to make a dear friend disappear. I’ll keep the spoilers light on when that happens in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but all you need to know is that our man Jason has been tasked with getting rid of a former contact’s car – plus all of their worldly possessions. Now, had I actually checked the trunk I would have seen a bright red gas can and then set the whole thing ablaze – unfortunately, I didn’t check the trunk. Instead, I drove the departed’s wheels straight into Leonida Bay in full view of witnesses. Now, our lad Jason is a wanted man looking to disappear himself. Camped out in a bush, the police scanner crackles to life. “Suspect is a white male wearing a baseball cap” – well, the cap's the first thing to go, then, as I leg it back to the Ganado. I could keep running and try to outpace the police’s BOLO, but GTA 6 offers a fair few options for escaping suspicion. Losing yourself in customisation and creating a well-stocked wardrobe has become well worth your while beyond simply looking sharp, and it’s now as much a part of your criminal arsenal as carrying a piece. I was already looking forward to playing dress up with Lucia, so when my new drug-shifting mum-doing-her-best pal Vicki points out the local vintage store, I can’t help but rub my grubby little gamer mitts together. But besides introducing more fashion options I’m personally inclined towards, chapter two also introduces new crimes to commit. Stick-ups are hit-it-and-quit-it criminal operations – brandish a gun, take the money, and then run. Lucia got her criminal start boosting cars when she was a young teen, so carjacking is a big, lucrative part of this chapter as well. These opportunistic crimes are a complementary contrast to chapter one’s more organised approach – but better yet, Lucia's working for herself rather than Jason playing passive errand boy. Dispatch advises to be on the lookout for someone matching my description. It's all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store. 29db6cc294a1.title: Rockstar North Chief Was Praying GTA 6's Big Story Reveal Stayed Under Wraps Ahead of Launch
29db6cc294a1.summary: Rockstar North has explained why it was so important that GTA 6's big early story reveal stayed under wraps before the game came out.
29db6cc294a1.content: Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6 . GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch. During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal. Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6 , it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of. “No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'” As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design . It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them. We aren’t simply committing crime for crime’s sake, but doing so with the prospect of being reunited with their son at the end of it. You can see why such a powerful and surprising narrative device would want to have been kept under wraps by Rockstar. It’s the first, and by no means the only, shocking revelation of GTA 6, all the more effective when witnessed firsthand. “We never were going to [reveal it],” Nelson explained. “It’s meant to shock. We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.” We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 4 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. af50b0c69262.title: Everything You Need To Know Ahead of The Delta Force Invitationals Grand Final
af50b0c69262.content: After last year’s inaugural event in Hangzhou, this weekend sees the Delta Force Invitational make its first move outside Asia, as an official competitive title at DreamHack in Stockholm, Sweden, from 27th-29th November. The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action. It’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows: Americas: Spacestation Gaming and GODL, via the 2026 RISE Series Americas Chinese Mainland: TES, RSG and IBG, via the Delta Force Pro League Korea: Nongshim RedForce, via RISE Series Korea Japan: FENNEL, via the 2026 Delta Force: Invitational Japan Qualifier Pan-Pacific: RX, MKK and ONIC via the Pan-Pacific Operations Cup S2 EMEA: Alliance and Fnatic, via the 2026 RISE Series EMEA Fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool. One core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted new fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match. Viewers who tune in to watch on Twitch via @DeltaForceGameOfficial or @DeltaForce_Esports can also bag a bunch of in-game rewards: 15 minutes: Armament Voucher 20 minutes: Calling Card - Delta Force Invitational 30 minutes: Standing Gear Ticket 45 minutes: AKM - Wandering Dragon 60 minutes: Action - Cheer Plus, GOTAGA, HutchMF, Summit1G, Panda and Timmy will also be streaming the matches on their channels during the event. There’s also a tonne of in-game incentives around the event, so be sure to login between the 11th November and 3rd December to get your hands on these: Log in for 1 day during the event - DFI-themed Spray Paint ×1 Log in for a total of 2 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2 Log in for a total of 3 days - Featured Keycard Copy Pack ×1 Log in for a total of 4 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2 If you correctly predict the outcome of the Invitational in-game, there’s a couple of other other rewards to be had: One of your selected teams reaches the Grand Final - Cosmetic Item: ASV - Northern Frontier - Assault Vehicle ×1 One of your selected teams wins the championship - Cosmetic Item: Overtime - AK 12 - Unstoppable (orange-tier weapon) In the two years since its launch, Delta Force has steadily gained momentum, with developers Team Jade determined to grow the tactical FPS into a globally recognised esports title. With three days of intense competition on the horizon, its future certainly looks bright. Delta Force is free to play and available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Android, iOS, Google Play, Epic Games Store, and Steam.

b1b188e9d883.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
b1b188e9d883.summary: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
b1b188e9d883.content: You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to. Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie. But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC . “As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?” When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.” I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage. That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. Still, with the staggering number of screenshots, videos, and everything else filling up social media feeds, anyone out of the loop would never know. I think much of this is due to just how many types of games Rockstar managed to cram into GTA 6. Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6. “Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began. “Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received. “I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.” “Happy Holiday's y'all.” Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer. Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.” Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.” Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game . bc322ad47a5a.title: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
bc322ad47a5a.summary: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
bc322ad47a5a.content: When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with. To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing. I spent most of my time in Cicia, a city of art, based loosely on Paris among other places, and lined with cobblestone streets and beatific brickwork architecture. Cicia was previously featured as a location in the mobile game Shining Nikki, and makes its 3D debut here. It’s a world where art nouveau, belle epoque and art deco collide, and home to the Cicia Art Academy where Miraland’s most promising students are taught lessons of art creation and appraisal by the finest tutors. When Nikki receives an invitation to study there, she and her catlike companion Momo embark on a new adventure of aesthetic discovery. But is everything at the academy truly as it seems? Some of the outfits in the update grant Nikki new skills. Unlock and craft the preppy four-star Leaping Breeze outfit to gain a higher double-jump and airborne dash abilities, while the much darker and sexier Night’s Hidden Side outfit allows Nikki to “bind” with objects around the environment (think Mario’s possession skill in Mario Odyssey) and use them to warp to hard-to-reach places. These new skills allow for a new level of verticality in Cicia’s map and dungeons, helping you explore the castle spires or negotiate intricate dungeon maps. You can also find a musket for long-range attacks (which is a new Whimtech item), and dress for the occasion in Cicia’s three-star, nine-piece outfit Song of Endless Youth. V3.0 also introduces a new outfit category, Star Crown Resonance. The Star Crown Resonance outfit named Where Stars Shine Again comes with a musket and staff, and is designed for tougher combat situations. With either weapon equipped, Nikki’s unused dashes are stored, and you can release them all at once or use them one at a time, creating a sort of combo system that deals more damage. While previous Infinity Nikki maps tended towards countryside locations, Cicia is a bustling city. Arriving by airship to take in the stunning views, Nikki and Momo step into a throng of students, teachers and residents, each with voiced dialogue to idly eavesdrop on as they prepare for a huge school festival, building an air of excitement as Nikki starts academy life. In this maelstrom of culture, recruiters for the drama club and literature club compete for Nikki’s attention. And then she meets Béatrice Laviolette. aadc52925da3.title: Rockstar North Boss Knew Some GTA 6 Players Would 'Reject' New Systems Like Criminal Profiles, but Insists 'You Can Still Do Whatever You Wanted to Do Before'
aadc52925da3.summary: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson knew some GTA 6 players would "reject" new systems like criminal profiles, but insisted "you can still do whatever you wanted to do before."
aadc52925da3.content: GTA 6 is by far the furthest Rockstar has pushed one of its games on a gameplay level. Perhaps nothing showcases that more than the criminal profile system ticking away in the background at all times, judging the way you act in its world as Jason and Lucia. No longer is Grand Theft Auto a sandbox where hedonism is widely encouraged, but a place that judges you for partaking in it. It’s a system that has caused much debate within the player base, with some feeling as if they’re being punished for how they traditionally played GTA games. It was something that Rockstar admitted to have been a little worried about when YouTuber TGG visited the studio months ago and claimed it was "going to change GTA." "I thought, 'Oh s**t, we’re in trouble,'" Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson told VGC . “But I said, 'It doesn’t change everything; it changes what GTA can be.' So for us, I think it opens a new range of choices and decisions for the player to make. You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options." Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow. The criminal profile system reacts to how violently you choose to act throughout GTA 6’s open world and missions. Opt for headshot kills over debilitating kneecaps? You’ll move away from the "professional" end of the spectrum towards "psycho" and eventually "irredeemable." From experience, though, I can confirm that it takes quite the effort to reach that point on the scale after going on one murderous rampage after the next. Which criminal profile you land on by the end of Jason and Lucia’s story will factor into which ending you get, but for the most part, it’s not something that necessarily needs to be playing on your mind at all times. My characters were considered “professional” at the end of my playthrough, and, believe me, I spilt my fair share of blood along the way. Nelson appears to know that not all players will necessarily be on board with changes to the GTA formula like this, though, and expects some to "reject this new stuff we’re offering." He does hope it may help to make people think differently about how they approach Rockstar games in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, though. "I hope it changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game," Nelson continued to tell VGC. "In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you’re setting these guys up as what they are. We were conscious of that. "Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They’re trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life. When you pick up with Jason, he’s still a criminal; he’s still getting in trouble with Donnie and all that, but he’s sort of been living this relatively criminal-adjacent existence." Whether GTA 6 feels like "classic GTA" or not is certainly a conversation to be had, but there’s no denying that the opening hours of Rockstar’s latest connects you to its characters more convincingly than the series has done in the past. Are you a fan of the criminal profile system? Let us know in the comments. Cyberleek, the infamous leaker behind many early GTA 6 gameplay clips, reportedly released the Xbox build of GTA 6 last week, and vibecoders have been attempting to port the game to PC since. Fueled by AI, progress has been swift, with clips showing GTA 6 running on PC at a higher frame rate than on console, and one video even showing basic multiplayer. Obviously, Rockstar Games, which will no doubt release GTA 6 on PC officially at some point, and parent company Take-Two will be watching the homebrew scene’s every move like a hawk. In the case of Project Leonida, Take-Two has already taken action. NotRexed was organizing and sharing work on a Discord group, and hosting their findings on a GitHub repository, when cease and desists from Take-Two hauled everything offline. NotRexed then took to social media to announce they'd decided to call it a day. “I quit guys. I’m sorry,” NotRexed said. “I really want to make cool stuff but every single time s**t happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid,” they said. “Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.” However, NotRexed has now returned, and promised to continue the project. “Ignore my other posts,” NotRexed said after changing their mind. “Something’s coming soon. Leonida is NOT dead. I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I’ll have some stuff to show all of you soon.” IGN spoke to NotRexed to find out why they’re doing this, whether they understand the risks, what they’ll do if they get in legal trouble, and what their parents think of it all. “It’s just a hobby of mine,” NotRexed said in a private message. “I started doing similar things with porting games to the web back in the start of 2026, and I’ve always just thought of it to be cool.” Before generative AI, NotRexed had no interest in porting games to other platforms, they said. But after finding out it was possible in 2025, they’re now taking on one of the most powerful publishers in video games. 886e18ef139e.title: Someone Is Making One of Baldur's Gate 3's Most Popular Villains Romanceable
886e18ef139e.summary: One of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash, could be romanceable soon thanks to this new fan-made mod.
886e18ef139e.content: Baldur's Gate 3 has no shortage of romances and romantic encounters, but not everyone in Faerûn is up for a smooch. When developer Larian was still rolling out updates, fans would often ask for more romances to be added, whether it be for Jaheira or Rolan, but it was never meant to be. One of the most popular requests was actually for one of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash. Larian was very much aware of this, and actually addressed these fans in the patch notes in 2024. "Listen, he’s a complicated guy who’s busy contemplating the minutia of death cult office politics," Larian said at the time. "Babygurl doesn’t have time to kiss." But now, a fan is stepping up, adding the Gortash romance that so many were asking for. TikTok user Equipouet has shared some clips from the mod, which is still a work in progress. It shows the player character being invited to spend time with Gortash, played by Lucius Malfoy actor Jason Isaacs, after his coronation in Act 3, all with new dialogue and animations. We're told that we'll be able to make our own choices when we meet Gortash, specifically whether we want to "charm him, keep him guessing, or walk away." So, if you really hate Gortash, you could also use the mod to let him down. Much more is teased for the mod, like a ball held by Gortash, letters to exchange with him, and "choices with consequences." There will also be changes to how the story plays out if your character is The Dark Urge, since it's in your backstory that you already have a history with Gortash. The mod is still being worked on, but the author says they will submit it for console release approval once it's done. That process can be lengthy, however, and there's no guarantee that it will pass the approval stage, especially if it's too bulky for console. In the meantime, Gortash kissers will keep having to use their imagination. Like us would-be Jaheira kissers. There are also plenty of other mods to try out, including a bunch that have Larian's seal of approval and can be installed within the game's own mod manager. Image credit: Larian.

c7e1a25fe1a2.title: Former Gran Turismo World Series Competitor Helped Tune GTA 6 Car Physics
c7e1a25fe1a2.summary: A former Gran Turismo World Series competitor helped Rockstar tune GTA 6's car physics.
c7e1a25fe1a2.content: A lot of people have complained about the Ganado, Jason’s starting car in GTA 6 , for being tricky to drive. The small pickup is a little unwieldy and prone to swinging out at the back end because it’s based on the Ford Ranchero, a rear-wheel drive whip manufactured between 1957–1979 in North America. While there are no licensed vehicles in GTA 6, cars are recognisable based on real-world counterparts, with small visual changes to make them legally distinct. But the accuracy doesn’t stop at the car model — it also extends to how they drive. That variety in handling is in part because Rockstar hired Lewis Bentley, a former Gran Turismo World Series competitor, to work on the vehicle physics team. Bentley announced the news in a now-deleted YouTube video. “We put the auto in the Grand Theft Auto,” he said from the driver’s seat of his Lotus Elise. Bentley is best known for qualifying for the final in the GT Sport World Tour event at the Nürburgring 24 Hours, in 2018. “Everyone on the physics team’s amazing,” he said in the same video. He claimed to have worked on GTA 6 for around three years in total, and is listed in the game’s credits as a developer in the physics department. Bentley isn’t the only gearhead who worked on the game, however. Rockstar North has its own in-house racing team , and they’re pretty good on the track — they won a team-based 24h Nürburgring event back in 2022. You can see this attention to detail in the game, both in vehicle handling models on cars and on the tracks. For the first time in the series, GTA 6 features a closed asphalt circuit called Gellhorn International Raceway, which stitches together a bunch of iconic corners and racing lines from some of the most famous real-world tracks in existence, turning them into the ultimate speedway. c73756746d47.title: BioWare Fans Hit Out at EA for Selling New Dragon Age Merch After Killing the Studio
c73756746d47.summary: A new Dragon Age hoodie is available on the BioWare Gear store, as EA continues to sell merch based on BioWare's now dead franchises.
c73756746d47.content: EA's decision to shut down BioWare sparked a mix of shock and sadness across the internet , with both fans and developers fondly remembering the many role-playing games the Canadian studio put out over the years. The Mass Effect community has been especially vocal , given that Mass Effect 5 was cancelled alongside the studio closure . But Dragon Age fans certainly aren't happy either, and they're making it known. Despite BioWare's closure, the BioWare Gear merch store is still being updated. A bunch of new items were added for N7 Day , but we just got a new Dragon Age merch drop too. For example, the Dragon Age Inquisition Seven of Swords Nightmare Hoodie features a piece of tarot card art that appears in Dragon Age: Inquisition. Better still, the art depicts fan-favourite character Duncan from Dragon Age: Origins. But given that we're only getting this hoodie after everyone who worked on the Dragon Age series lost their job, it isn't sitting well with fans. "Do not give #EA the privilege of royalties on IP they have killed, and will not sell or forfeit," one fan said . "If you want your voice heard and want to #SaveDragonAge and #SaveMassEffect, EA needs to reckon with the consequences of their bad financial decisions. #BoycottEA and licensed merch." "Save Mass Effect. Save Dragon Age. Dragon Age was failed massively by EA. You destroyed what Veilguard could have/should have been because you pushed for it to be live service then backtracked. You never gave Dragon Age the chance it deserved," another person replied to the BioWare Gear Store's post promoting the hoodie . "No studio, No Game = No money," Olarcadia said on X / Twitter . "What you're doing is a pure lack of respect." "It's so cute how you think putting out merch is going to make us hate you any less," onedcdame agreed. "Keep it. BioWare is closed, we're not giving you any of our money EA," replied SignWithBlood. "You should offer to sell back the IP to the founders, including the BioWare brand and name," added @inkpot__gods. "We bought merch to support the devs who made the games we loved; you fired all the devs and stopped making those games, so there’s no one left for us to financially support," said LouEaglesham. It appears that the community plans to boycott EA's continued use of BioWare's IPs, at least until it allows a team of devs to make a new game in these universes. Right now, both Dragon Age and Mass Effect are on ice. Dragon Age fans in particular have a lot to be upset about. The last game in the series, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, largely failed to impress the community. But it has long been known that the game languished in development hell and suffered from various changes in direction. Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah recently shared the original vision for the fourth Dragon Age game , before EA allegedly mandated that it had to be a live service. EA would then go on to allow the game to be retooled as a single-player RPG, but The Veilguard had to be built from the bones of this live service work, meaning the developers didn't have time to return to this original outline. It remains to be seen what EA does next with the Dragon Age series. EA is not in the habit of selling off IP, but if enough fans are boycotting the merch, it leaves EA without much to do other than just sit on it.

215b6d9817ec.title: On Top of Everything Else, GTA 6 Is a Solid Stealth Sandbox
215b6d9817ec.summary: I came to GTA 6 for its wild car chases and explosive shootouts, but its the really solid stealth that has me hooked.
215b6d9817ec.content: This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games. Grand Theft Auto is a boisterous, brash series full of loud characters and louder explosions. GTA 6 continues that tradition for many of its main story beats, chaining showy set-pieces into lethal car chases, but in my 35 hours roaming Leonda I've found plenty of chances to engage with its surprisingly robust stealth system. In some cases, it even feels like Rockstar specifically designed areas with sneaking and silencers in mind. Illegal operations are lucrative robbery opportunities dotted around the map that hide cash, jewellery, drugs, and unique items – cars, weapons, watches – guarded by armies of enemies. I struggled with them early on: shooting my way to the valuables attracted GTA 6's menacing police, curtailing my heists before I could grab all the loot and forcing me to flee across entire counties while a chopper buzzed overhead. Now, I treat these scenarios like stealth vignettes, my goal to remain hidden for as long as possible. I've screwed silencers onto my weapons and prioritized headshot precision over spraying power, carrying a pistol alongside either a tactical rifle or a sniper. My shotgun is purely for backup, just in case. Skirting around these hideouts reveals hidden entrances. For Janjak's Garage in Vice City, for example, you can mantle a dumpster in a neighbouring alley to reach the garage's sheet metal roof. Out West, on the edge of Port Gellhorn, you can avoid the main gates of the giant Brooks Boatworks and slip through holes in the fence. Stealth detection is intuitive. Crouching reduces noise, sightlines feel realistic, and you'll be warned by a yellow arrow over an enemy's head before they fully spot you, allowing you a window to nip back into cover. Knives silently slice enemies' open or you can choke them quietly from behind. And if you need space, you can whistle from cover to draw foes over, or throw bottles to distract them. It's classic stealth game fare. But I've found that guns with silencers are actually the best option because they avoid the risk of an enemy spinning around at the wrong moment and catching you, knife raised. They mask shots almost completely: I've stood close to enemies and shot at others without being detected. Not everything in GTA 6 adopts Rockstar's general pursuit of realism. Illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. Clusters of enemies are tricky because as soon as you shoot one, the others will spin and look for you. Here, I use focus mode to slow time and pop a series of headshots, plink, plink, plink. Three bodies thud simultaneously. I feel like prime Sam Fisher. High ground is vital and from the right vantage I can survey the area, plan my route, and pick off enemies from distance. I always clamber to the loftiest point and use the D-pad to tag visible hostiles, which tracks them through walls. In a pinch, focus mode will highlight enemies through walls too, although only if they're nearby. Some of the level design feels like it's steering you down this silent route. Back at the Boatworks, the first thing I saw after sneaking in was a platform lift to the roof of the main warehouse, high above every enemy. A drop in the ceiling led me to an empty top floor – I've seen this trick repeated in other hideouts, so I always look for ladders or other ways to reach the roof. In the bigger compounds, staying silent for longer than a few minutes is a real challenge. No matter how many times I ran the Boatworks (I saved before I tried, and reloaded when I failed) I was always eventually spotted by some unaccounted-for enemy. b76290a7b131.title: I Tried to Get Six Stars in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game
b76290a7b131.summary: We tried to get six stars in GTA 6 by firing just one bullet and broke the game.
b76290a7b131.content: If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out. When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive. We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. Creeping cannibalistic thoughts pushed to one side, we walked back inside knowing our work was done. This public execution, perhaps rightfully, attracted a police patrol car to the restaurant, of which Lucia did not take kindly to their arrival. Her love for Jason knows no bounds, up to and including unloading full machine gun magazines into any cops who want to arrest him. And who were we to stand in her way? Letting her take control of the situation was then required, honorably moving Jason behind the indestructible cover of an industrial refrigerator. Sporting an armoured vest just in case any stray bullets or shrapnel found their way around the corner, it was then time to hunker down in the kitchen beside that thick metal fridge, out of view of law enforcement. Crucially, this fast food establishment’s kitchen does not have a door leading outside, meaning the threat of flanking cops was neutralised. Luckily, they didn’t seem to spot the drive-thru window, which would’ve handed them a clean shot. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet? And there we sat for a good 45 minutes as Lucia angrily gunned down anyone brave enough to step into the restaurant. No more food would be served today, only death. The red of discarded hot sauce packets replaced by the blood of the fallen. The crunch of hard shell tacos drowned out by the crack of broken bones. All in the name of science. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet? Well, not this time. We could’ve sat here forever, bravely hiding behind a fridge while our partner slaughtered hundreds. Lucia was invincible, rounds of ammunition sinking into her skin to no effect. She had no shortage of ammo herself; with an unlimited pool of lead to reload from, she could’ve done this all day, and all for us. If that isn’t true romance, I don’t know what is. Day turned to night, and the restaurant workers diligently remained kneeling behind the counter and cowering for the whole sordid ordeal. The problem is, our aggressors just… stopped. After a period of quiet, we chose to break cover and wander outside, only to be met by several non-aggravated members of law enforcement staring blankly at us. We had seemingly confused them with our methods of madness. Because we’re so dedicated to the cause here at IGN, we tried all over again.
